clue.text: Angry shooting?

parts.note: someone angry is cross
shooting is firing, so fire

explanation.surface: A question about gunfire let off in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is a playful picture of shots fired in a temper, which is also how the two halves of the answer build it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossfire is gunfire coming from two or more directions at once; the clue jokingly reads it as bad-tempered shooting.

clue.text: Let rip with Edwin

parts.note: a rip or tear is a rent
Ed is a short form of the name Edwin

explanation.surface: Someone tells Edwin to go ahead and let rip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let rip' looks like one phrase; 'Let' is the definition and 'rip' gives RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a property is to have it rented out to a tenant.

clue.text: Make good in a nimble way

explanation.surface: Advice to make good by moving nimbly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the rare adverb formed from supple, pronounced differently from the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply a want is to make good a deficiency; as an adverb, the word also means supplely, with nimble flexibility.

clue.text: Thin film replaced before sly pupil leaves

indicators.note: the letters of the word film are put back in a different order
the pupil goes away, so its letter is dropped from the word sly

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a pupil driver

explanation.surface: A flimsy film is swapped out before a cunning schoolchild walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' turns FILM into FLIM; 'leaves' takes L (learner, a pupil) out of SLY to leave SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy is insubstantial or weak, as a thin excuse is.

clue.text: Irresolute aunt's remarkable act of bravado

indicators.note: remarkable suggests something extraordinary, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An indecisive aunt performs a striking feat of daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges the fifteen letters of IRRESOLUTE AUNTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning a revolver with one live round and firing at your own head is the ultimate reckless show of daring.

clue.text: Aren't big words used in this light conversation?

definitions.text: Aren't big words used in this light conversation?

parts.words: Aren't big words used in this light conversation?
parts.note: a chat about trivial things is imagined as one using only little, not big, words

explanation.surface: A question whether casual chatter avoids long words.
explanation.definitionFit: Chit-chat on trivial subjects, the opposite of weighty discussion, is light conversation.

clue.text: Electrical device of endless size with gold finish

indicators.note: finish puts the gold piece at the end of the answer
endless means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: capacity is a measure of size or volume
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gadget, with no limits on its dimensions, given a golden coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims CAPACITY to CAPACIT; OR, the heraldic word for gold, comes at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A capacitor is a component that stores electric charge in a circuit.

clue.text: Brother goes to racecourse in Essex!

parts.note: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse that stages the Grand National

explanation.surface: A sibling heads off to the races in an eastern county.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the English racecourse home of the Grand National steeplechase; Essex is a county north-east of London, and the answer is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Braintree is a market town in the county of Essex.

clue.text: Demon wind damage

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
a wind is moving air

explanation.surface: A devilish gale causes destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or harm it.

clue.text: Smartest being most likely to take a photograph?

definitions.text: being most likely to take a photograph?

explanation.surface: The best-dressed person is also the keenest photographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means stylishly smart; it is also jokingly read as most inclined to snap, that is take a picture.

clue.text: It will not pass the acid test

definitions.text: It will not pass the acid test

parts.words: It will not pass the acid test
parts.note: the idiom for a decisive trial is read literally: a substance that fails a chemical test for acidity, being its opposite

explanation.surface: Something is declared sure to fail a decisive trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A base that dissolves in water is chemically the opposite of an acid, so a test for acidity comes out negative.

clue.text: Article is becoming true-to-life

indicators.note: becoming means turning into, so these letters change into a new word

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is turning into a faithful portrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifelike, faithful portrayal is a realistic one.

clue.text: Harsh way I caught Rex inside

indicators.note: inside means the king's letter goes within the other pieces

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
CT is a scorecard abbreviation for caught in cricket
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone harshly describes catching a dog named Rex indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the king's letter after the abbreviation for street. CT for caught is the scorecard form, rarer than plain C.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict regime is severe, unbending and stern.

clue.text: Salt from messy shop public house consumed

indicators.note: messy means jumbled up, so the letters of shop are scrambled

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for a public house
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Seasoning taken from an untidy store in a pub that has been eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A phosphate is a salt of phosphoric acid, as used in fertilisers.

clue.text: Six balls needed before test defeat

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A bowler needs one more over before losing a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is six balls bowled, and a Test is a full international MATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To overmatch an opponent is to be too strong for them and beat them.

clue.text: Order to decorate before middle of week

parts.note: to garnish a dish is to decorate it

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of the word week

explanation.surface: An instruction to put up decorations ahead of Wednesday.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses garnishee as a verb, to order the seizure of a debtor's money.
explanation.definitionFit: To garnishee is to serve a legal notice ordering a third party to withhold money owed to a debtor.

clue.text: Flow of writing

parts.note: what flows from a pen when one writes

explanation.definitionFit: The fluid in a pen runs onto the page as words are written.

clue.text: Frosty, alternately bitchy

indicators.note: alternately takes every other letter of the word bitchy, from the second

explanation.surface: Someone is cold and, by turns, catty.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy manner is cold and unfriendly, as a frosty one is.

clue.text: Captured soldiers leave man shortly

indicators.note: leave means the soldiers depart, so their letters are dropped

parts.note: captured means taken
TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: Prisoners taken, the troops briefly leave a man.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken is a short form of the man's name Kenneth.

clue.text: Be slightly mad when it hasn't been tightened up properly

definitions.text: when it hasn't been tightened up properly

explanation.surface: A loose fixing is likened to a touch of madness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means be a bit crazy; literally it describes a fastener that has not been fully driven home.

clue.text: Some modesty once over there

indicators.note: some of the words modesty once supplies a run of letters

explanation.surface: A bit of former bashfulness is spotted in the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap in modestY ONce.
explanation.definitionFit: Yon is an old or dialect word for yonder, that place in the distance.

clue.text: Run second run-off

parts.note: to run off copies is to print them

explanation.surface: A race decided by a second heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run-off' looks like a deciding race, but here it means printing copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a short, fast run.

clue.text: I am after tax

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
post is a Latin prefix meaning after

explanation.surface: Someone declares that they are seeking a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a levy or duty imposed by authority.

clue.text: Slow play

parts.note: a musical movement performed at a leisurely tempo

explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the Italian tempo marking for a slow movement.

clue.text: Distracted viewers I leave avoid a crash

indicators.note: distracted suggests confused, so the letters of viewers are rearranged after the I goes

explanation.surface: Inattentive spectators leave just in time to escape an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' signals that I comes out of VIEWERS before 'Distracted' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers swerve, veering suddenly, to dodge a collision.

clue.text: Retreat after reaching peak?

explanation.surface: A mountaineer turns back once at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbdown is a backing down from a position; literally it is the descent that follows reaching the top.

clue.text: Here's a removal vehicle!

indicators.note: removal suggests moving things about, so the letters of here's a are shifted around

explanation.surface: Someone announces the arrival of a removal van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removal' suggests a furniture van but signals moving the letters of HERES A; the whole clue then describes a vehicle that removes the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the car that carries a coffin away at a funeral.

clue.text: Tactics used by robust member?

parts.note: robust means strong
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A question about the methods of a hefty member of some group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a person in a club but means a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong-arm tactics use force or bullying, as a powerful limb might.

clue.text: About to come back from school shop first with Australian food

indicators.note: first puts the school shop at the front of the answer

parts.note: a tuck shop sells sweets and snacks at a British school

indicators.note: to come back means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone returns from the school tuck shop with antipodean grub.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuck shop is a British school's snack shop. 'to come back' reverses the word for about, and 'first' puts the shop ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucker is Australian slang for food.

clue.text: Warship one ruins

explanation.surface: A naval vessel is the thing that wrecks things.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast naval vessel; literally it is one who destroys, or ruins.
